title: Thinking Outside the Bots: Human Ideas in AI's Semantic Blind Spots Are Not Inferior
abstract: arXiv:2610.17324v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI-generated outputs are frequently perceived as highly creative, but also tend to be more similar to each other (homogenized) than human ideas. Does the human heterogeneity that extends beyond AI reflect valuable thinking that AI misses? Alternatively, is greater human heterogeneity driven by lower-quality ideas and less effective thinking that AI avoids? We developed Expansion of Divergent Generative Expression (EDGE) to map AI's semantic "blind spots" by assessing how strongly/weakly individual human ideas were represented in a task-matched AI semantic comparison set. Specifically, we compared human-generated vs. AI-generated ideas across three open-ended tasks: college admissions essays, alternative uses for everyday objects, and interpersonal advice. Across all three tasks, human responses extended into semantic regions sparsely covered by AI outputs. These distinctively human responses showed no meaningful deficits in creativity,

translated_title: 跳出机器人的思维：AI语义盲区中的人类想法并不逊色
translated_abstract: AI生成的输出常被认为具有高度创造性，但与人类想法相比往往更加彼此相似（同质化）。超出AI范围的人类异质性是否反映了AI所遗漏的有价值思维？抑或是，更大的人类异质性源于质量较低的想法和AI所规避的低效思维？我们开发了“发散性生成表达的扩展”（EDGE）方法，通过评估个体人类想法在与任务匹配的AI语义比较集中的表征强弱程度，来绘制AI的语义“盲区”。具体而言，我们在三项开放性任务中比较了人类生成的想法与AI生成的想法：大学入学申请文书、日常物品的替代用途以及人际建议。在所有三项任务中，人类的回应都延伸到了AI输出稀疏覆盖的语义区域。这些独特的人类回应在创造力方面没有表现出明显的缺陷……
tldr: 本研究开发了EDGE方法来绘制AI的语义“盲区”，发现在大学文书、物品替代用途和人际建议三项开放性任务中，人类想法均延伸至AI输出稀少覆盖的语义区域，且这些独特的人类回应在创造力上并不逊色。
en_tdlr: The study develops EDGE to map AI's semantic "blind spots," showing that across three open-ended tasks—college essays, alternative uses, and interpersonal advice—human responses extend into semantic regions sparsely covered by AI outputs, and these distinctively human ideas show no meaningful deficits in creativity.
